topSignals.title: Bernstein initiates Bloom Energy at Market Perform / $276 — first bulge-bracket cautious note (June 16)
topSignals.text: Bernstein SocGen initiated coverage with a neutral stance and $276 target vs. BE trading at ~$281 (+240% YTD). Praise: "quickest to develop" generation tech in its coverage universe. Concerns: no clear free cash flow pathway independent of one-time contract timing, and manufacturing scale-up visibility needed. First major research house to set a price target below current price — a notable counterweight to the 74% Buy consensus. (Investing.com: Bernstein initiation; Yahoo Finance: RBC still bullish at 240% YTD)

topSignals.title: EIA June STEO (June 16) raises Henry Hub 2026 full-year avg to $3.60/MMBtu
topSignals.text: Up from $3.50/MMBtu in May STEO and above the $3.34/MMBtu figure cited in this digest's June 10 issue. Driver: oil-price-linked associated gas production growth (+3.3% US output in 2026). At $3.60/MMBtu, SOFC fuel input cost rises to ~$0.034–$0.042/kWh at 55–60% LHV efficiency — roughly $3–5/MWh upward LCOE pressure. LCOE model flag. (Rigzone: EIA raises HH forecasts; EIA June STEO)

topSignals.title: Doosan Enerbility: 1,480 MW CCGT steam turbines for unnamed US big-tech Texas DC (May 27 — first digest coverage)
topSignals.text: Follow-on to March 2026 first North American contract; four 370 MW steam turbines for a single hyperscaler campus, deliveries sequentially through 2029. Competing power signal: large gas-fired CCGT is being contracted in parallel with SOFC by the same customer tier. SOFC's near-term advantage (90-day deployment) holds — CCGT 3 years out. Strategically notable: Doosan simultaneously supplies Ceres Power-licensed SOFC stacks, competing in both markets. (Seoul Economic Daily; Turbomachinery Magazine)

items.text: Quiet day. No new announcements from Bloom, Ceres, Elcogen, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi, or Topsoe.
Quiet day. No new SOFC deployment announcements. Existing confirmed pipeline (Oracle 2.45 GW, Nebius $2.6B, Brookfield $5B, AEP $2.65B, Equinix 100 MW+) all previously reported.

FERC RM26-4 ruling imminent (expected on or around June 18): As of June 17, no formal order published. FERC committed to end-of-June action; ruling widely anticipated today/tomorrow. Cost-allocation model (developer-funded vs. socialised transmission costs) is the key variable for SOFC behind-the-meter economics. Monitor ferc.gov/rm26-4. (National Law Review: industry anticipation)

Germany EnEfG: July 1 deadline in 14 days. New DCs commissioning from July 1 must achieve PUE ≤1.2 at commissioning and ERF ≥10% (rising to 15% in 2027, 20% in 2028); 100% renewable electricity from July 2027. No new compliance amendments or guidance issued today. (Orrick: EnEfG draft amendment)

Doosan Enerbility 1,480 MW CCGT for Texas big-tech DC (May 27 — first coverage): See Top Signals #3. Follow-on steam turbine supply contract; combined-cycle deliveries through 2029. Largest single CCGT commitment identified for a US hyperscaler data center to date.

Fermi America Project Matador (Amarillo TX, up to 11 GW): Geotechnical work started; GE TM2500 gas turbines (157.5 MW) bridging first phase targeting 2026; AP1000 nuclear reactors (Doosan/Hyundai E&C partnership) expected online ~2032. Largest planned energy/data campus globally. No SOFC impact before 2030+; long-term nuclear alternative signal. (Data Center Dynamics: Fermi America; Carbon Credits: Project Matador)

Bernstein initiates BE at Market Perform / $276 (June 16): See Top Signals #1. BE at ~$281 (+240% YTD); first major research house with a sub-market price target, signalling valuation debate is opening.
RBC bullish on BE at 240% YTD: Maintains positive stance, argues AI demand pipeline justifies continued multiple expansion. (Yahoo Finance)

FuelCell Energy Q2 FY2026 (period ending April 30) additional detail: Revenue $35.59M (–5% YoY); operating loss $77.91M including $42.57M non-cash impairment on the Groton Project (separate from the $64.5M SOFC exit impairment reported in the June 15 digest). Combined Q2 impairments ~$107M. FCEL shares ~$17 (market cap ~$1.16B). (24/7 Wall St.)
Quiet day. No new papers, patents, or national-lab results.

lcoe.text: Henry Hub 2026 full-year revised to $3.60/MMBtu (EIA June STEO, June 16) — MODEL UPDATE: Previous digest baseline was $3.34/MMBtu (June 10 STEO) for 2H26. EIA's June 16 update revises 2026 full-year average to $3.60/MMBtu (up from $3.50/MMBtu in May STEO). 2H26 specific: $3.34/MMBtu. 2027 raised to $3.46/MMBtu (from ~$3.18 previously). At $3.60/MMBtu, SOFC fuel cost ≈ $0.034–$0.042/kWh (55–60% LHV), adding ~$3–5/MWh vs. prior baseline. LCOE range revises to approximately $133–210/MWh (from $130–205/MWh) unsubsidized; CHP-adjusted lower bound ~$123/MWh. (Rigzone)

CCGT build-time datapoint (NEW context): Doosan steam turbine deliveries confirmed through 2029 for a May 2026 order — 3-year lead time for large CCGT equipment. Quantifies the opportunity window for SOFC before competing gas-fired capacity reaches operation.
